title: Heuristic pricing matrix for smart routing (worksheet)
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet captures a pragmatic, heuristic pricing matrix for smart routing decisions. The goal is to produce a small-rule decision surface that engineers can map to runtime routing policies (fallback tiers, region selection, spot vs on-demand) without requiring real-time ML scoring. This is intentionally opinionated and tuned for three common workload archetypes we see in production.

Quick summary (one-line):
- Use a prioritized cost SLO + degraded-latency tolerance to decide: prefer spot in lower-priority regions for short-chat workloads, prefer reserved/on-demand for latency-sensitive streams, and use a two-step fallback (region fallback -> capacity tier fallback) with quantized thresholds.

Assumptions (for the numbers below):
- Token mix: short-chat median 20 tokens response; long-completion median 600 tokens.
- On-demand GPU cost per 1M tokens (effective, amortized): us-west-2 on-demand = $16.40, us-east-1 on-demand = $15.70, eu-west-1 on-demand = $18.90.
- Spot is on average 45% cheaper but with 3–8% preemption probability for our target instance types; effective cost per 1M tokens = on-demand * 0.55 + failover-penalty.
- Reserved (dedicated) capacity blended cost = on-demand * 0.70 (committed discount + utilization).
- Failover penalty = additional 12% cost when a spot-preempted request falls back to on-demand (re-execution/KV-loss/latency tail).
- SLA tolerance tiers: gold (p99 latency < 200ms), silver (p99 < 600ms), bronze (p99 < 1500ms).
- Network/egress differences between regions are ignored for initial heuristics; we call out when it matters.

Compact heuristic matrix (rows are workload archetypes, columns are routing preference ordered):

Archetype A: short-chat (PLG UX), low latency required, high QPS
Routing order: local-region-reserved -> local-region-spot (if cost target) -> remote-spot (if capacity) -> remote-on-demand fallback
Rationale: short responses favor batching/caching; reserved capacity keeps tail latency predictable. Spot is OK when cost pressure but add early fallback timeouts (50ms) to avoid user-visible stalls.

Archetype B: long-generation (batch inference, e.g., doc summarization), tolerant latency
Routing order: remote-spot -> remote-spot-burst -> local-on-demand -> dedicated-reserved (scheduled overflow)
Rationale: long tokens favor cheaper compute and can absorb occasional preemptions; failover is expensive but amortized across tokens.

Archetype C: streaming or function-call (low p50 but strict p99)
Routing order: local-reserved -> local-on-demand -> remote-reserved -> remote-on-demand
Rationale: avoid spot for streaming unless we have a warmed, pre-empt-resilient KV cache strategy.

Illustrative cost table (effective $ per 1M tokens) — heuristic numbers for model selection logic:

Region | On-demand | Spot (raw) | Spot (with failover adj) | Reserved
us-east-1 | $15.70 | $8.60 | $10.50 | $11.00
us-west-2 | $16.40 | $9.02 | $11.02 | $11.48
eu-west-1 | $18.90 | $10.40 | $12.26 | $13.23

Interpretation: route to the lowest expected-cost slot that satisfies the workload's latency SLO. For short-chat gold traffic, cost target must be within 1.2x of on-demand local; otherwise prefer local-reserved even if slightly higher cost because user-visible latency impacts MAU.

Simple expected-cost formula used for routing heuristics: 
ExpectedCost = BaseComputeCost * (1 + PreemptProb * FailoverMultiplier) * (1 + DataTransferPenalty)
- PreemptProb: empirical per-region/per-instance value (spot preempt rate).
- FailoverMultiplier: fraction of additional compute & retry cost (we use 0.12).
- DataTransferPenalty: 0.0 for intra-region, 0.02–0.07 for cross-region depending on egress.

Sensitivity scenarios (run these quickly in spreadsheet before applying rules):
- High preempt scenario (spot preempt 12%): spot adjusted cost increases sharply; avoid for p99-sensitive routes.
- High token length scenario (+5x tokens): prefer spot/remote even for silver SLA because absolute cost delta dominates latency tradeoff.
- Heavy cold-start KV loss: if cache miss rate expected >30% on fallback, add 8% to failover penalty.

Sample micro-rules to encode in runtime config (short list to implement quickly):
1) Per-API-route cost_target_multiplier (default 1.0). If candidate expected cost > cost_target_multiplier * local_on_demand_cost then deprioritize.
2) Fallback order always preserves region-preference: prefer same region capacity tiers before going cross-region.
3) Spot candidate must set a preempt-timeout: if no token output within T_spot_timeout (default 50ms for short-chat, 200ms for long-gen) then trigger fallback to next tier.
4) Reserve a small percentage (5–10%) of local-reserved capacity for gold routes to avoid cascading fallbacks during preemption storms.
5) KV cache TTL policy: for spot-backed routes, raise prefix caching TTL by 20% to reduce re-compute cost on preemption.

Example worked calculation (short-chat gold in us-west-2):
- local_on_demand = $16.40 per 1M tokens. cost_target_multiplier=1.15 -> threshold = $18.86
- candidate: local_spot adjusted = $11.02 -> passes threshold, but preempt risk => p99 degrade risk. If route is gold, prefer reserved at $11.48? Wait. Reserved is $11.48 which is cheaper and predictable -> choose reserved. If reserved fully utilized, then local_spot is acceptable with preempt protections.

Operational controls & telemetry to ship with the heuristic:
- Expose per-route counters: chosen_tier, preempt_events, fallback_latency, cost_estimate_at_choice.
- Alert: if fallback_rate > 0.5% over 1h for gold routes -> auto-expedite (increase reserved buffer).
- Weekly report: cost-savings vs SLA-change by route (show delta if spot usage increased 10% vs baseline).

Implementation notes (engineering constraints):
- Keep heuristics as a small JSON policy blob: {route_pattern, archetype, cost_target_multiplier, prefer_regions, fallback_order, spot_timeout_ms, reserved_buffer_pct}. This keeps runtime decision logic simple and auditable.
- We need a daily job that refreshes per-region spot preempt rates and recomputes adjusted spot costs used by policies.

Open questions & TODOs:
- Quantify egress penalty per customer region (APAC vs EU vs NA) and include in the expected-cost formula.
- Experiment: optimistic KV-checkpointing on spot workers (warm-kv replicas) to reduce failover penalty — run A/B on batch workloads.
- Validate Reserved blended cost assumptions with finance for new instance SKUs (Q4 pricing changes likely).

Decision checklist for product review:
- [ ] Confirm cost baselines with Finance (tag: JIRA-OPT-289).
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks to route decision path (PR: redwood/serve#4127).
- [ ] Run 2-week experiment on short-chat silver routes using 30% spot to measure p99 impact.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative on failover penalty to avoid chasing marginal savings that increase user-visible latency.
- If you want a richer probabilistic optimizer later, we can export this worksheet to a small linear-programming solver using daily spot/latency stats. For now, the simple matrix wins for explainability and rapid rollout.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Priya: finalize matrix and run finance sync (due 2025-11-19).
- Liam: prototype JSON policy shape + feature flag (due 2025-12-01).
- Renata: baseline telemetry and fallback_rate SLO (due 2025-11-30).
- Ethan: draft A/B test spec for short-chat silver (due 2025-11-26).

-- end of worksheet --
